abstract: the increasing demand for sustainable agricultural practices has led to a growing interest in the use of microbiological fertilizers as eco-friendly alternatives to chemical inputs. this study investigates the effect of microbiological fertilizers on the growth and yield of wheat (triticum aestivum l.) under field conditions. experimental plots were established with four treatment groups: control (no fertilizer)
and a combined treatment of chemical and microbiological fertilizers. parameters such as plant height

and soil microbial activity were measured throughout the growing season. the results demonstrated that the application of microbiological fertilizers significantly enhanced wheat yield and improved soil biological health compared to the control. furthermore
the combined use of chemical and microbiological fertilizers yielded the highest productivity
indicating a synergistic effect. these findings suggest that microbiological fertilizers can serve as an effective component in integrated nutrient management strategies
contributing to higher crop yields and sustainable soil management. keywords: wheat

the abundance of major microbial groups

showed high ecological plasticity. among ten isolates
